scenes.say: Is your HTML just a bunch of divs, or does it actually tell browsers and humans what each part means? Why bother with semantic HTML?

scenes.label: header
scenes.sub: <header> marks the start of a page or section.
scenes.say: A header element marks the start of your page or a section. It tells everyone, including screen readers, what’s important.
Use nav for navigation, main for the main content, article for standalone pieces, and footer for the bottom of your page.
Here’s an article element. It wraps a news item, making its purpose clear to browsers and assistive tech.

scenes.question: Should you use <div> for everything?
scenes.right: No. Semantic tags improve accessibility and SEO.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for the div trap. Semantic tags make your code more accessible and help search engines understand your site.
